original_question: Is the gene associated with Pyle disease also linked to diabetes?

final_qi.question: Is the gene associated with Pyle disease also linked to diabetes?
final_qi.long_answer:
Pyle disease (metaphyseal dysplasia, Pyle type) is caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in the SFRP4 gene, which encodes secreted frizzled-related protein-4, a modulator of Wnt signalling.  Independent of its role in bone, SFRP4 has repeatedly been implicated in glucose metabolism:  
• Human studies have shown that higher circulating SFRP4 concentrations predict future development of impaired glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes, and variants in or near SFRP4 have been associated with diabetic phenotypes in several cohorts.  
• Experimental work demonstrates that SFRP4 is expressed in pancreatic islets, where increased SFRP4 activity suppresses insulin secretion, whereas reduced SFRP4 activity can improve glucose tolerance in animal models.  
These findings establish a recognised link between SFRP4 and diabetes risk/pathophysiology.  Therefore, the gene responsible for Pyle disease (SFRP4) is also linked to diabetes.
